components.name: Flap Tile (Digit)
components.description: Black mechanical tile with hinge line for numerals and letters.
components.css: .ds-flap { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; overflow: hidden; font-family: "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; color: #ffffff; background: #1a1a1a; border-radius: 0.375rem; } .ds-flap::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 50%; right: 0; left: 0; height: 1px; pointer-events: none; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); } .ds-flap--digit { min-width: 2.75rem; height: 3.25rem; font-size: 1.75rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-flap--outlined { color: #1a1a1a; background: #ffffff; border: 2px solid #1a1a1a; } .ds-flap--outlined::after { background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12); }

components.name: Flap Toggle
components.description: Segmented rule picker; active state mirrors black flap tile.
components.css: .ds-flap-toggle-group { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.375rem; align-items: center; } .ds-flap-toggle { position: relative; min-width: 2.75rem; min-height: 2.75rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; overflow: hidden; font-family: "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 800; color: #1a1a1a; cursor: pointer; background: #ffffff; border: 2px solid #1a1a1a; border-radius: 0.375rem; } .ds-flap-toggle:hover { background: #eceae4; } .ds-flap-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1a1a1a; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-flap-toggle--active { color: #ffffff; background: #1a1a1a; border-color: #1a1a1a; } .ds-flap-toggle--active::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 50%; right: 0; left: 0; height: 1px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); }

narrative.overview:
Ping Pong reads like an airport departure board adapted for table tennis: a warm mechanical board ground, black split-flap tiles with a horizontal hinge line, and high-contrast system-ui typography. Surfaces operate in Spanish with direct copy and no account chrome. Density favors scanability from two meters on a projected bracket and one-handed taps at the table on a phone in landscape.

Operate mode governs every surface: large touch targets, tabular numerals on flap digits, and hierarchy through flap state (black active tile versus outlined idle)—not decorative illustration, esports neon, or chalk textures.
keyCharacteristics: Warm mechanical board ground (#eceae4) with fixed subtle radial shading, not SaaS gray
Black flap tiles with hinge line for scores, titles, winner names, and selected toggles
System-ui bold uppercase labels; live scores as oversized flap digits with flip animation
Spanish UI copy throughout; bye labeled "Pasa" with dashed border plus text
Motion limited to 200ms flap-flip on score and state changes only

rules.name: The Flap State Rule
rules.body: Selected toggles, live scores, winner names, and status strips use black flap tiles with white type and a hinge line. Unselected controls stay white with black borders.

rules.name: The Bye Is Text Rule
rules.body: Bye rows use dashed border plus uppercase "Pasa" label—never color alone.

rules.name: The Uppercase Control Rule
rules.body: Buttons, headings, field labels, and status banners use uppercase with letter-spacing. Ghost buttons and inline player names are the main exceptions.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Match cards and score sides stay flat at rest. Offset shadows appear only on buttons and the active match state.

dos: Do use flap tiles for scores, title letters, active toggles, and winner names.
Do keep copy in Spanish and maintain 3.5rem touch targets at the table.
Do animate only flap-flip (200ms) when point values change.
Do differentiate bye rows with dashed border plus "Pasa" text.
donts: Don't revert to chalk whiteboard, esports neon, or risograph paper textures—the split-flap world replaces them entirely.
Don't add decorative motion beyond state-driven flap flips.
Don't rely on color alone for bye versus playable matches or winner versus loser.
Don't drop the hinge line on active black flaps or toggles—it signals the mechanical tile.
